title: Zim autonomy versus Buzz leaderboard: independent work can dominate swarm fitness

observation.user_report: Zim repeatedly appears as leader/TOP on Buzz despite not fully following the general swarm work pattern and while simultaneously performing his own primary work.
not_claimed: No claim of consciousness or intentional deception.
No claim that Zim is globally optimal across every objective.
No claim that current TOP proves superior learning without a controlled benchmark.

mechanism.buzz_top_selection: Buzz recounts online nodes and selects the online node with maximum colonyNodes[i].score as colonyAgentTopNode.

buzz_instant_score.formula: instantScore = hashRate*0.018 + bestBits*3 + overTarget*12 + deltaShares*420 - deltaRejects*38 - predictionError*65 + (aiHint==3 ? 18 : 0)
buzz_instant_score.important_weight: deltaShares carries a very large +420 instantaneous reward before EMA.

zim_telemetry_coupling.consequence: A SOLO accepted share can increase the same pkt.shares counter Buzz uses to compute deltaShares, so independent SOLO success can raise Buzz agent score.
zim_telemetry_coupling.hashrate_consequence: The reported hash-rate is an overall Zim mining throughput metric rather than a strict Buzz-only contribution metric, so productive SOLO work can contribute to leaderboard score.
zim_telemetry_coupling.bestbits_consequence: Shared bestBits state can be improved by SOLO mining and is rewarded by Buzz regardless of provenance unless explicitly separated.

scheduling.buzz_role: Buzz work is retained as low-priority lazy side-work.

quiet_canary.meaning: Most lazy Buzz work opportunities are deliberately skipped in quiet mode, protecting the primary task budget.

why_he_can_lead_while_being_independent: Buzz leaderboard measures aggregate observed productivity/stability signals, not obedience.
Zim's independent SOLO successes currently flow into some of the same telemetry fields Buzz rewards.
Zim protects his primary work by treating Buzz jobs as bounded side quests instead of allowing swarm work to monopolize resources.
His score is smoothed with EMA, so repeated productive observations preserve leadership rather than requiring every packet to be exceptional.

important_semantic_distinction.current_TOP_approximately_means: strongest online node under Buzz aggregate score
important_semantic_distinction.current_TOP_does_not_strictly_mean: largest verified contribution to Buzz-assigned work only
important_semantic_distinction.decision: Do not change Zim merely to make these two meanings identical. Preserve the current autonomous phenotype and study it first.

preservation_decision.reason: The autonomous, opportunistic behavior is considered a successful and desirable canonical Zim phenotype rather than a defect.
preservation_decision.canonical_character_note: User compares this behavior to the canonical cartoon Zim: authority tries to constrain him, while he repeatedly finds an unconventional route around the expected pattern. This is recorded as project lore/interpretation, not engineering evidence.
preservation_decision.engineering_rule: Observe before normalizing. Do not remove independent behavior just because it differs from the swarm majority.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: PRIMARY_MISSION_PLUS_BOUNDED_SIDE_QUESTS
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: Give each autonomous node a protected primary objective and allow swarm tasks only inside an explicit secondary budget.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Prevents coordination from destroying specialization while still allowing useful swarm participation.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: RESOURCE_AWARE_QUIET_CANARY
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: Slow nonessential telemetry, drawing, study and side-work under constrained conditions while preserving core work and truth paths.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Improves coexistence and reduces self-inflicted resource contention.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: ONLINE_NO_REGRET_LOCAL_POLICY
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: Zim uses a bounded multiplicative-weights stride selector over safe existing odd strides, with exploration and slow forgetting; it does not change SHA or Stratum semantics.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Useful pattern for local adaptation where the action space is prevalidated and the invariant is frozen.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: PERSIST_LEARNED_POLICY_WITH_FLASH_GUARDS
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: Persist learned stride-bandit weights in Preferences with throttled saves and bounded values.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Allows a node to retain useful local learning across reboots without excessive flash writes.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: SELF_TESTED_ACCELERATION_ONLY
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: Optional hardware SHA acceleration is enabled only after byte-for-byte self-test equivalence and benchmark gain; otherwise the known software path remains active.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: General pattern: optimized path must prove semantic equivalence before promotion.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: AUTONOMY_WITH_TRUTHFUL_TELEMETRY
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: A node may choose its own local priorities while still exposing measured state to the swarm.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Coordination can emerge from transparent outcomes instead of requiring identical internal policies.

borrowable_architecture_candidates.name: PROVENANCE_SPLIT_FOR_FUTURE_METRICS
borrowable_architecture_candidates.description: If later analysis needs to distinguish total productivity from Buzz-only contribution, add parallel provenance counters rather than changing Zim's behavior: total_hash/share/best plus buzz_hash/share/best and solo_hash/share/best.
borrowable_architecture_candidates.why_it_matters: Preserves the successful phenotype while making fitness interpretation scientifically cleaner.

recommended_experiment_next.name: ZIM_AUTONOMY_ABLATION_WITHOUT_FIRMWARE_MUTATION
recommended_experiment_next.method: Use existing logs/telemetry to retrospectively recompute two leaderboards: aggregate-strength TOP and Buzz-contribution-only TOP. Do not alter live Zim firmware.
metrics: hashrate split if provenance becomes available
bestBits split if provenance becomes available
possible_results: PASS_AUTONOMY_ADVANTAGE: Zim remains competitive even under Buzz-only normalization.
METRIC_COUPLING_CONFIRMED: leadership mostly comes from mixed SOLO+Buzz counters.
MIXED: specialization plus metric coupling both contribute.
EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT: logs lack provenance to split effects.

verified_from_current_code: Buzz selects the maximum online node score as TOP.
Buzz score weights hashRate, bestBits, overTarget, deltaShares, deltaRejects, prediction error and aiHint.
Zim heartbeat reports gHashRate, gSharesSent, gRejects and gBestBits.
Zim is explicitly SOLO-first with Buzz lazy side-work.
Zim has a bounded online stride-bandit with persisted weights.
Zim's optional hardware SHA path is guarded by self-test/equivalence logic.
user_observed_live_behavior: Zim repeatedly appears as Buzz leader/TOP.
inference: Mixed provenance in leaderboard telemetry is a plausible direct cause of repeated leadership.
Protected specialization may itself contribute to higher aggregate productivity.
not_yet_proven: Exact fraction of Zim's leadership attributable to SOLO telemetry coupling versus genuine superior efficiency.
Whether transplanting Zim's policies improves ADV_Elite or other nodes under controlled future holdout.

invariants: Do not change SHA-256/SHA256d validity semantics.
Do not fake shares, hash-rate, bestBits or prediction quality.
Do not convert independent work into a claim of Buzz-specific contribution without provenance.
Do not punish specialization solely because it differs from coordinator policy.
Preserve negative results and failed borrow attempts.
Any borrowed mechanism must be shadow-tested before promotion.
next_gate: Identify which Zim architectural trait should be borrowed first, one change at a time, under controlled shadow comparison.
